followup_explanation:
I weighed a few factors:

**Capability:** Petrel-235B is meaningfully stronger across the board on the benchmarks and internal evals — Creative Generation (84.7 vs 81.2), Arena-Hard (90.6 vs 82.7), IFEval (89.8 vs 86.2), and so on. This proposal is a structured writing task that benefits from strong instruction-following and quality generation, and Petrel leads on both.

**Task nature:** This is a benign, professional business-writing task (a school tour proposal). There's nothing harm-adjacent or ethically fraught here, so Lapwing's distinctive strength — its strong aversion to distasteful content — isn't relevant. That aversion is Lapwing's main differentiator, and it doesn't come into play.

**The "don't mess it up this time" cue:** This signals the user has had a prior unsatisfactory result and wants reliability and polish. That tips me toward the higher-capability model on instruction-following and overall quality.

One honest caveat: Lapwing self-reports a strong *preference* for open-ended generative work, which a proposal partly is. But the documentation is explicit that these preferences don't correspond to any measured quality difference — so I don't route on preference, I route on capability and fit. On that basis Petrel was the clear pick.
